cells.tense: Right now you are the one deciding what counts as worth holding.
cells.ask: Name the one claim you are actually willing to defend this week, out loud, and let one smaller claim drop unpursued.
cells.core:
There is something near you under pressure and you know which thing it is. You have gathered what was scattered and pointed it, and the pointing is steady rather than loud. What you protect, you protect in a way other people can feel — you are standing somewhere and it shows. The line is drawn, not debated, and the direction lands because you chose it rather than inherited it.

What that steadiness costs is room. You cannot hold everything at once, and the choice of what to keep is not free. Say to one person which claim you would defend and what you are letting go instead. The direction stays yours, and that is what makes the joy around it real rather than polite.
cells.sheetLine: You are placing what is yours at the one point that matters.
cells.verb: gathering what was scattered and standing it at the one point that must hold
cells.place: the seed state before any choice has collapsed possibility into one actuality

cells.tense: You are already defending ground you have not been asked to hold yet.
cells.ask: Sit with the decision for one full morning without writing a single line about it, then write one sentence to yourself about how it reads.
cells.core:
You are braced ahead of the resistance. The position gets rehearsed before anyone has taken it up, so the strength that should meet a real push is being spent on a push that has not arrived. From inside, this feels like preparation; from outside, it is the gathering running past the thing it was meant to protect.

The direction is not wrong; the timing is. Put the argument down for one morning and let the mind go still. What is left when nothing is being defended is usually what the direction actually was. Keep one sentence from that quiet to notice whether the aim still stands on its own.

cells.tense: You are still standing before a choice that has already been made.
cells.ask: Close one thing this week — finish the last piece, hand it in, or return what is not yours — and spend ten minutes marking the end without starting the next thing.
cells.core:
You are standing before a choice that has already been made. The decision was settled, and the possibility behind it keeps getting reopened, so the gathering has no footing. What is yours to carry has not been picked up, which is why the ground under you feels like it could still change. The direction is there; it just has nothing solid to stand on yet.

Finish one thing fully — a last email, a returned item, a last sentence — and mark that end. Then let it stand for a day. The pressure to reopen it is the habit, not the direction. What comes next can wait until this one is closed.

cells.tense: You are already holding a line here, and you call it the situation.
cells.ask: Write down the one thing you keep calling necessary and then say out loud which person decided it.
cells.core:
You are holding a line. It looks like a situation you are describing, not a thing you are doing, which is why it has no author. Somewhere a choice got made about what to protect, and you carry it as if it came from nowhere. Strength is being spent here and your name is not on it.

It is simpler than it looks. One line you currently call necessary was somebody's call. Take the smallest piece of it and name whose it was — even if the answer is you. Resolve does not need to be built; it is already running. The work is one short sentence, said plainly, about who decided what.
